headline: Vote to remove historical commissioner Milo Martinez fails, 2 to 5, with two present
summary: The vote followed public comments Martinez made about enforcing short-term rental rules. Under the city charter, removing a commissioner early required five votes. Members also sent rules for Charlotte-Forton Park to committee and approved $163,099 for the High Street Park renovation.
decisions: Granted National Grid's request to install one single-owned pole on Bridge Street at Flint Street.
Approved paying a $23,477.11 prior-year invoice from EJ Prescott from the DPS water and sewer budget.
Approved $163,099 in short-term capital funds for the High Street Park renovation project.
Approved accepting a $2,000 donation from Beverly Peabody Lodge 1309 for Salem Veterans Services.
Approved accepting two donated works of art for display at Salem High School.
Removal of Historical Commissioner Milo Martinez failed, with 2 yes, 5 no, and 2 present.
The motion to reconsider the vote on removing Milo Martinez failed.
Referred amendments to the 2023 outdoor dining policy to the Committee on Community and Economic Development, co-posted with the Committee of the Whole.
Approved free parking at city-owned lots, garages, and on-street spaces on listed holiday days from November 27 through December 24.
Approved waiving up to 30 days of late fees on unpaid parking fines from November 27th to December 23rd, 2026, for food donations.
Approved creating an ad hoc committee to screen applicants for Salem City Clerk.
Approved a resolution supporting the unionization of workers at the Peabody Essex Museum and urging the museum to recognize the union.
Referred the ordinance on rules for Charlotte-Forton Park to the Committee on Government Services, co-posted with the Committee of the Whole.
Approved first passage of an ordinance removing resident-only signs from the parking lot next to the High Street Playground on Pratt Street.
Approved a resolution to accept state grants for High Street Park.
Referred the battery energy storage systems zoning ordinance to the Planning Board for a joint public hearing.
Approved receiving and filing the committee report on Skipper on-demand ride program contracts.
Denied the recommendation to withdraw the rooftop wind energy zoning ordinance without prejudice.
Referred the roof-mounted wind energy systems ordinance to the Committee on Ordinances, License, and Legal Affairs, co-posted with the Committee of the Whole.
Approved the outdoor lighting ordinance on second and final passage.
Approved the parking ordinance on Cleveland Street on second and final passage.
discussion: Milo Martinez removal: Public speakers praised Martinez's work on the commission and asked that he stay. Members split over whether his October 8 comments on short-term rental enforcement broke his oath of office, and whether he had enough notice to prepare.

Charlotte-Forton Park rules: Public speakers opposed the ordinance and asked that it go to committee. Members raised concerns that fines and some restrictions would affect unhoused people, and asked how the rules compare with those for Salem Common.
Peabody Essex Museum union: Public speakers said the workers seek collective bargaining for living wages, benefits, and more input in decisions that affect staff.

Rooftop wind ordinance: The sustainability and planning directors asked the council to withdraw the ordinance over a possible conflict with the battery storage ordinance. Members said it would go to committee anyway for changes the planning board suggested.
Outdoor dining policy: Members said they wanted more committee discussion on rules for outdoor dining, including year-round use and design standards.
